resolutions.researcher_notes: The live opec.org URL 301-redirects to the opec.org homepage (confirmed via curl) — the known ASB dead-link gotcha. Recovered via Wayback (2025 snapshot, verified live 200); pdftotext extraction of the recovered PDF shows OPEC's Table 9.9 'Main gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2016' lists 'Bu Attifel/Intisar (2)' (two lines, 34in/10in) as a current operating gas pipeline connection — the automated substring screen can't match plain text inside a compressed PDF stream, so this was confirmed by manual pdftotext read rather than the url_verifier content check. Independent second source: Petroleum Africa (Dec 2017 trade-press article, live, verified) reports the Abu-Attifel gas plant resumed processing and that 'the entire natural gas produced from Abu-Attifel Field will be processed through this plant, where it will be pumped as dry gas to the 103 A field [Intisar]' — confirms the pipeline was actively carrying gas as of late 2017, independent of OPEC. No source suggests the line has since been shelved/cancelled.

Recovered dead ASB2013 live link via Wayback (verified live 200 by url_verifier; content confirmed by pdftotext, which the automated substring screen can't do on compressed PDF text). OPEC ASB2013 Table 4.10 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2012' lists: 'Bu-Attifel/Intesar (103A)   Eni Oil   82.46 [mi]   10 [in]   258,425   na' — the capacity figure 258,425 is an EXACT match to the sheet value. FLAG (unit caveat): the table's capacity column header reads '(1,000 scm/yr)', i.e. the source's own units are thousand-scm/yr, not scm/yr as GEM's CapacityUnits states — so either GEM's CapacityUnits label is off by a factor of 1,000 (actual capacity would be ~258.4 million scm/yr) or the raw number needs rescaling; the digits themselves are exactly sourced, only the unit label is in question. Only one source located with this specific figure (single OPEC edition) — tier medium, not corroborated by a second independent source, so flagging rather than upgrading to high.

OPEC ASB2017 Table 9.9 gives the Bu Attifel/Intisar connection as '2 x 82' miles (82 miles per line, 10in and 34in). 82 mi x 1.609344 = 131.97 km, matching the sheet's 131.96 km almost exactly (rounding). ASB2013 Table 4.10 gives a more precise 82.46 mi for the same connection (=132.68 km) — a ~0.7 km / 0.5% difference from the sheet value, likely just OPEC's own rounding drift between editions rather than a real length change; not treated as a contradiction. No non-OPEC source with an explicit length figure for this specific line was found, so both supporting figures trace to the same institution (OPEC ASB, different editions) rather than fully independent origins — tier medium. Could not find any independent (non-OPEC) length source; no working ref existed previously (class UNRESOLVED in brief) — this is now REFS_ADDED via the Wayback ASB2017 recovery.

Petroleum Africa (trade press, verified live) directly states all gas produced at the Abu-Attifel field is processed and pumped onward as dry gas toward the 103A/Intisar field — confirming Bu-Attifel Field as the fuel source feeding this line. USGS Bulletin 2202-F ('The Sirte Basin Province of Libya', verified live 200; content confirmed via pdftotext, which the automated substring screen can't read off compressed PDF text) independently identifies Abu Attifel as one of the giant Nubian-Sandstone oil/gas fields of the eastern Sirte Basin and maps it directly adjacent to the Intisar (103-A/103-D) fields — an independent academic-geological source corroborating Bu-Attifel Field as the origin field. Two independent origins (trade press + USGS) agree.

USGS Bulletin 2202-F (verified live 200; content confirmed via pdftotext, not the automated substring screen, which can't read compressed PDF text) places both 'Abu Attifel field' and 'Intisar (103-A)/Intisar (103-D)' within the eastern Sirte Basin province and shows them as neighboring fields on its structural map (fig. 1) — directly supporting StartState/Province=EndState/Province='Sirte Basin' and both endpoint field names. Petroleum Africa (independent trade-press source) confirms the flow direction and field names: gas from Abu-Attifel is processed then pumped toward the '103 A field' (Intisar), operated by Zueitina Oil Company. Two independent origins agree on both endpoints and the Sirte Basin location.

NOT a double-count — evidence points to two real, parallel gas pipelines, not one line entered twice. Internal comparison: P1858 (34in, capacity 4,134,806) and P6714 (10in, capacity 258,425) share the identical length (131.96 km) and identical start/end (Bu-Attifel Oil Field -> Intesar Oil field, Sirte Basin). OPEC ASB2013 Table 4.10 ('Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2012', p.~74-75, recovered via Wayback, pdftotext-confirmed) lists them as TWO SEPARATE table rows with different operators: 'Bu-Attifel/Intesar   Mellitah Oil and Gas   82.46mi   34in   4,134,806' and 'Bu-Attifel/Intesar (103A)   Eni Oil   82.46mi   10in   258,425' -- exact match to P1858 and P6714 respectively, down to the capacity figures. OPEC ASB2017 Table 9.9 (2016 data, recovered via Wayback) independently corroborates this across a later edition, listing the connection as 'Bu Attifel/Intisar (2)' -- explicitly '(2)' = two lines -- '2 x 82mi', diameters '34, 10', joint owner field 'Mellitah Oil & Gas, Eni Oil' (i.e. one line per operator). Two OPEC editions four years apart, independently compiled, agree that this is a twinned/parallel pipeline pair (same corridor, different operators/diameters/capacities), not a single pipeline double-entered. Recommend: NOT a candidate for merging/removal; if anything, GEM's Owner/Operator data for these two rows should be checked to confirm P1858=Mellitah Oil & Gas and P6714=Eni Oil, matching the OPEC operator split (out of scope for this ref-only shard).
